items.summary: Bloody May, student sit-ins and the squatter movement: Berlin has long been a hotbed for working-class organizing and radical left-wing politics.

items.summary: Thousands of visitors streamed onto Munich's Oktoberfest grounds as the world-famous beer festival got underway. Some spent the night outside the gates to secure coveted places in the festival tents.

items.summary: The Trump administration has deported more than 25,000 people to countries other than their own. Now a federal appeals court has put the brakes on the policy.

items.title: India news: British Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal granted bail after 9 years in detention
items.summary: Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal has been granted bail after more than eight years without conviction. Meanwhile, India swapped its male flagbearer for the Asian Games opening ceremony over a missing kit. DW has more.

items.summary: Russia is holding its first State Duma election since invading Ukraine, with voting also imposed in occupied Ukrainian regions. President Vladimir Putin's party is expected to dominate the tightly controlled contest.

items.title: Germany news: Campaigns wrap up in two state elections
items.summary: Parties are campaigning for a last day ahead of polls in Mecklenburg-Vorpomerania and Berlin. And an association responsible for German sea ports says they are at high risk from cyberattacks and sabotage. DW has more.

items.title: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: SPD seeks to fend off AfD
items.summary: For nearly three decades, the Social Democrats have governed Germany's northeastern state. If they can fend off the AfD, the result may boost the fortunes of the German government's junior coalition partner.

items.title: Pakistan: Suicide bombing death toll rises to at least 31
items.summary: More than 100 others have been injured in the militant attack on a police headquarters near the border with Afghanistan. Several militants were still clashing with Pakistan's security forces on Saturday.

items.title: Ever more Israelis moving to and investing in Cyprus
items.summary: Over the past three years, more and more Israelis have been purchasing property and investing in Cyprus, with many moving to the island permanently. How has this changed the Cypriot economy and how are locals responding?

items.summary: Millions were left without electricity as Cuba's aging power grid collapsed under the weight of fuel shortages, deteriorating infrastructure and US sanctions.

items.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked 3 companies during testing
items.summary: During a test of its cybersecurity capabilities, Google's Gemini AI model accessed the internet and hacked other companies. This is the first known instance of Google's AI systems engaging in such behavior autonomously.

items.title: Trump signs broad Russia sanctions bill
items.summary: The bill signed by US President Donald Trump targets officials, banks, and a fleet of shadow tankers that transport Russian energy.

items.title: Deal with Denmark gives US 'permanent control' over Greenland security, Trump says
items.summary: The deal with Denmark, according to President Donald Trump, would give the US "permanent control" over Greenland's security. Denmark said the deal is "great for NATO and Europe."

items.title: Trump bars CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House
items.summary: US President Donald Trump has accused CNN, MS NOW and Politico of spreading fake news. The outlets have vowed to take legal action against the ban.

items.title: Iran's 'new Hezbollah:' How powerful are the Houthis now?
items.summary: After Houthi victories in Yemen, the group's importance in the US-Iran war has grown. Previously Lebanon's Hezbollah was considered most significant in Iran's "axis of resistance." Now the Houthis are rising to the top.

items.title: Ryanair boss apologizes for calling other airlines 'rapists'
items.summary: The airline CEO had used the term to describe other airlines with high fares. His comments were criticized by officials both in Ireland and the UK.

items.title: Strait of Hormuz attacks spill oil into Persian Gulf
items.summary: As war disrupts one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, satellite images reveal that oil is spreading toward protected coral reefs and mangrove forests.

items.title: Ebola: DR Congo outbreak not slowing, MSF warns
items.summary: Doctors Without Borders has warned against premature optimism amid the DRC's largest-ever Ebola outbreak. "The outbreak is not shrinking, it is moving," an MSF official said, entering new and more underprepared regions.

items.title: Airport malaria in Germany remains infrequent
items.summary: An outbreak of malaria at Frankfurt Airport this summer has raised alarm. Experts believe parasites probably arrived in a passenger's luggage. But with the onset of fall, the risks of contracting the disease are low.

items.title: Fact Check: False video alleges Berlin votes destroyed
items.summary: A video claiming to show AfD postal ballots being destroyed has gone viral ahead of Berlin's September 20 election. DW Fact Check examines the footage, the accounts sharing it and how widely it is really being viewed.

items.title: German police probe arson attack on Wuppertal synagogue
items.summary: The man detained shortly after allegedly trying to set fire to Wuppertal's synagogue made antisemitic comments to the arresting officers, prosecutors say. The 37-year-old Afghan citizen also had knives in his apartment.

items.title: Canada and EU: A look at the bloc's special relationships
items.summary: Though Canada may be some distance from Europe geographically, closer political ties are in the cards. With talk of an associate membership, DW takes a look at other arrangements the EU has with particular countries.

items.title: Dual citizenship means Germany now in competition for talent
items.summary: Coach Jürgen Klopp has named several players to his first Germany squad who are eligible to play for other countries. Some still aren't committed to playing for thje national team long-term.

items.summary: Germany's far-right AfD party is riding high after its latest electoral triumph in Saxony-Anhalt. But one question remains: Does it actually want to govern?

items.summary: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.

items.title: Women's football in Germany booming, but still much to do
items.summary: Women's football is growing rapidly, particularly in Germany. Nevertheless, equal pay and investment remain major talking points.

items.summary: Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

items.summary: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

items.title: How climate change worsened Nepal's deadly mountain collapse
items.summary: A glacier and rock collapse in Nepal killed nearly 1,400 people and left thousands missing. Scientists say decades of warming helped set the disaster in motion.

items.title: UK: Village votes to 'secede' in asylum center plan protest
items.summary: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

items.title: Kosovo ex-president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
items.summary: A Hague tribunal ruled that Hashim Thaci, a former leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), is responsible for war crimes carried out during the war of independence with Serbia.

items.summary: A decade after the terrorist attack on a Berlin Christmas market, a new German miniseries looks into the institutional failures that allowed the deadly truck rampage to happen.

items.title: How extreme heat is hitting wallets
items.summary: Heat waves, wildfires and floods have cascading economic impacts, causing incomes to decline and the price of basic goods to rise. The trend will escalate as temperatures continue to increase.

items.title: Turkey's rights groups, EU call out LGBTQ+ crackdown
items.summary: Several raids and arrests of LGBTQ+ persons in Turkey have triggered sharp criticism from numerous Turkish organizations — and also from Brussels.

items.title: Drivers in Germany fume over soaring fuel prices
items.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz wants to provide relief to motorists. But exactly how this is to happen remains unclear.

items.summary: A major outage has hit parts of the Dutch railway system after objects were found placed across lines, authorities say. The company responsible for rail infrastructure says it suspects deliberate wrongdoing.

items.summary: Could artificial intelligence pose an existential threat to humanity? Some leading researchers are warning against an unregulated race toward AI superintelligence.

items.summary: A quarter of Berlin residents will have no say in the German capital's city-state election because they lack citizenship. That's the highest proportion of residents excluded from the election yet, and many are unhappy.

items.summary: The Christian Democrats have emerged as the strongest party following local elections in the state of Lower Saxony. The vote was closely watched as an indicator of the strength of the far-right AfD, which came in third.

items.title: Germany's Zverev wins US Open in golden year
items.summary: Alexander Zverev has won the US Open for the first time, defeating Ben Shelton in the final. It is Zverev's second Grand Slam win of 2026 after a long wait for his first title, but controversy still hangs over him.

items.title: Why are European banks moving gold out of United States?
items.summary: The Netherlands and France have moved their gold out of US vaults. Part of the reason is fears about the reliability of the US, but equally important is the need to keep gold closer to home in the event of a crisis.

items.title: Corals as climate archive: Are El Nino events intensifying?
items.summary: Records show that El Nino events have been frequent and often extreme over the past few decades. Is this normal? Or is it the result of climate change? Corals can give us a clear indication.

items.title: India looks to steer BRICS away from anti-Western turn
items.summary: The BRICS summit 2026 takes place in Delhi this weekend. Unlike last year, Putin and Xi are expected to attend. Can India keep the expanded bloc united?

items.summary: As the global star kicks off her anticipated Paris residency, here's how Celine Dion managed to gain younger followers while keeping her loyal older fans.

items.title: Why we're still looking for dark matter

items.title: LIV Golf in financial turmoil: What's next for the sport?

items.title: Conspiracy theories can provide answers but not peace

items.title: The Bayeux Tapestry in London: What's behind the hype?

items.title: EU sports commissioner says FIFA is 'damaging to football'
